title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into a high-traffic scenario during Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco without sufficient battery reserves to handle extended gridlock. At least a dozen vehicles became stranded on city streets as severe congestion and unplanned road closures consumed more power than the system was built to manage. This failure occurred at the point of deployment, where the vehicles could not adapt to conditions outside their normal operating parameters.

The incident shows a system evaluated for typical traffic patterns but exposed to an exceptional event it could not endure. Waymo's roadside assistance teams had to physically recover the vehicles, indicating the system lacked either predictive capacity to avoid such scenarios or fallback power reserves for contingencies. The company states it is now evaluating resilience improvements, suggesting this failure was not anticipated in the original design.

It is not established whether the vehicles could have been prevented from entering the affected area, whether real-time traffic prediction could have rerouted them in advance, or what specific power requirements would have been necessary to survive the duration of the gridlock.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, several Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on city streets when their batteries drained during severe traffic congestion. Video footage verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve its resilience during major traffic disruptions.

The gridlock also affected other aspects of the situation. One Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. A passenger witnessed her autonomous vehicle unexpectedly drive during fireworks chaos, while another person spent nearly two hours stuck in traffic. This incident follows a December power outage that previously caused Waymo vehicles to malfunction at nonfunctional traffic lights. San Francisco's mayor and Department of Emergency Management are now discussing traffic management for future events with public and private partners.
